title: Behaviour is held by structure first; live runs only at judgment, never in CI
situation: Live behavioural runs became the build loop: builders tuned the architect's shared text against live agents, round after round, about 500 runs and 68 million tokens in one cut 7 round, and passed examples were re-run after shared changes. The operator, 2026-10-12: anything that can be held by structure should be; live tests run only during development, never in CI; development converges only what failed. Replaying saved runs verifies the checks and the shipped judging machinery, not the agents' text.
decision: (1) A behaviour an agent can be made to show through an act the harness checks is held that way and tested deterministically, never by live runs. (2) CI runs the deterministic suite and replays of saved runs only; no live agent runs in CI. (3) Builders iterate against saved runs; live runs happen at judgment, within a fixed budget per behavioural concept per cut, and again when the underlying model or harness changes. (4) The deterministic suite runs whole every round; live runs cover only what failed and what the change touches, and a batch is never re-run on unchanged work. (5) A behaviour that spends its live budget without holding is split off, never tuned further.
consequences: Supersedes in practice the per-round live sampling of 0088(3); applies to every later cut.
